title: Descartes Colloquium: Max Weber: The value of value-free science
speaker: Paul Ziche (UU)
location: UCU, Locke Hall, room C1.1, Campusplein 16-10
description: Descartes Centre Colloquium on history & philosophy of science (replaces the UPAC Colloquium this week). Hybrid; e-mail dc-colloquium@uu.nl for the Teams link.
abstract: Max Weber is standardly read as championing the idea that science (in the broad sense) should be "value-free". But this is rather strange: Weber is also emphasizing very strongly that decisions as regards values are essential for basically all of our actions, and certainly for actions in the domain of the sciences. This paper will present these two (apparently) diverging strands in Weber's thinking, will discuss which strategies might lie behind the one-sided reading of Weber as championing value-free science, and present some suggestions for how to assess and present the value of value-free science – as everything in Weber, this discussion is also about politics, so it will also be discussed how his ideas and concepts relate to an ever more politicized debate about science.
